glosses: Gonfler et distendre l’abdomen par des flatuosités.

examples.text: Certains fourrages mangés trop verts météorisent les bestiaux.
Si on palpe le ventre on le trouve tendu et météorisé.

glosses: Se dégrader, subir une érosion, être érodé.

examples.text: Les strates minces, de quelques centimètres, du fait de l'hétérogénéité, se météorisent plus facilement que les strates épaisses (1-5 m), sans feuilletage, massives.
Les cendres contiennent des minéraux qui se météorisent, c'est-à-dire qui se dégradent en libérant des nutriments dans le sol à long et à moyen terme, comme la silice, le fer ou le potassium.

glosses: To get an overdistended rumen, talking of a ruminant.
To fill soft substance with gas, water, etc.; to cause to swell.
To become distended; to swell up.

examples.text: if a Person of a firm Conſtitution begins to bloat, and from being warm grows cold, his Fibres grow weak, Anxiety and Palpitations of the Heart are a ſign of weak Fibres

glosses: To fill with vanity or conceit.

examples.text:
1675, John Dryden, Prologue to Circe by Dr. Davenant
Encourage him, and bloat him up with Praise

glosses: To preserve by slightly salting and lightly smoking.
To increase to an excessive amount.

examples.text: In the UK, the fraction of electricity generated by nuclear plants has slid steadily downwards, from 25% in the 1990s to 16% in 2020. Of the five nuclear stations still producing power, only one will run beyond 2028. Hinkley Point C, the first new nuclear plant in a generation, is being built in Somerset, but its cost has bloated to more than £25bn.
